extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for the USPTO to effect a reciprocal transfer of a registered practitioner to disability inactive status based on a state court order; covers notice, opportunity to respond, publication, legal effect, and ancillary administrative actions (account dissociation, duties, notice to agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statutory/regulatory authority when ordering reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status; base action on those provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal transfer is based on a transferring jurisdiction's order transferring the practitioner to disability inactive status (here, Colorado Supreme Court order in People v. Ramon L. Pizarro, No. 21PDJ059 (Colo. Dec. 30, 2021)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state court's order transferring a practitioner to disability inactive status provides the factual/legal basis for USPTO reciprocal transfer under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must mail a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.29' notifying the respondent of the Request and providing an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal transfer based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be mailed (here by certified mail) and must inform the respondent of the grounds available to oppose transfer; allow the regulatory response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing method and record of service
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. provided) and the Final Order was mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the most recent address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certified mail (with receipt) and document service; maintain certificate of service reflecting compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was given an opportunity to file, within thitty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform respondent of the specific time window to respond and the regulatory basis for opposition; (note: adopt the correct regulatory period in practice—this document shows 'thitty (40) days').

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was published in the Official Gazette (dates provided: May 23, 2023 and May 30, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish the Notice and Order in the Official Gazette as part of the notification/public record process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination standard if no response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, it may be determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d) and that transfer to disability inactive status is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond can support a finding of no genuine issue of material fact and justify reciprocal transfer under § 11.29(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transfer on practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is transferred to disability inactive status, precluding him from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for an indefinite period until further Order of the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transfer to disability inactive status results in ineligibility to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Official Gazette notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the practitioner (name, registration number, city), state that the Director ordered transfer to disability inactive status, state the practitioner is ineligible to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, or other non-patent matters, identify the state-court order and date that formed the basis, and cite applicable statutes/regulations (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient identifying information, basis for the action (state decision citation and date), applicable legal citations, and a reference to where disciplinary decisions are publicly available (FOIA reading room link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions and decisions regarding transfer to disability inactive status are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a public access point (FOIA reading room) for disciplinary records and include link in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public pursuant to §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the transfer and the reasons for the transfer to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly notify relevant state enforcement agencies, courts of admission, and the public as required by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transferred to disability inactive status, enforce the regulatory duties (e.g., notification obligations, case/counsel transfer obligations) specified in § 11.58; the order references compliance without restating the duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administratively remove the practitioner from customer numbers and electronic accounts to prevent practice before the Office while inactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to Customer Numbers until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar the respondent from acquiring or being associated with customer numbers while on disability inactive status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Certificate of Service is required showing mailing of the Final Order by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and include a certificate of service indicating compliance with service rules and the address used under § 11.11(a).
